mainTopic: The time of the afternoon תמיד: its Torah source, why it moves earlier on ערב פסח, and the מחלוקת about ערב פסח that falls on שבת
overview: The משנה gives three times for the afternoon תמיד. On an ordinary day it is slaughtered at 8½ hours. On ערב פסח it is slaughtered at 7½, so the קרבן פסח can come after it. On a Friday ערב פסח it is slaughtered at 6½, so the פסח can be roasted before שבת. רבי יהושע בן לוי derives the 8½ time from 'בין הערבים'. רבא objects: if 8½ were a Torah law, the time could not be moved earlier on ערב פסח. So רבא says the Torah time begins right after midday. The 8½ hour is just a delay to leave room for other offerings, and that delay is shortened on ערב פסח and dropped completely on a Friday ערב פסח. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree about the schedule when ערב פסח falls on שבת. אביי explains the dispute as being about the order of the מוספין and the בזיכין. רבא explains it as being about whether we worry that the meat will spoil while it waits to be roasted after שבת.

steps.title: The normal time for the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that on a regular day the afternoon תמיד is slaughtered at 8½ hours and offered on the מזבח at 9½ hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The afternoon תמיד is slaughtered at eight and a half hours into the day, and it is offered on the מזבח at nine and a half hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the basic daily schedule for the afternoon תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day there are two תמיד offerings, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. This line fixes the afternoon one: slaughter at 8½ hours, finish on the מזבח at 9½. This is the baseline that the rest of the משנה adjusts.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The daily communal offering, brought every morning and every afternoon
Is slaughtered
Is offered, meaning its parts are put on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hours' here are counted from the start of the day, about sunrise, not from midnight. So 8½ hours is about 2½ hours after midday, roughly 2:30 PM on an equal-length day. These are seasonal hours (שעות זמניות), each one 1/12 of the daylight.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The daily offering is slaughtered
at eight and a half hours,
and is offered at nine and a half hours.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On an ordinary day the afternoon תמיד is slaughtered at 8½ hours and offered at 9½ hours.

steps.title: On ערב פסח the תמיד moves one hour earlier
steps.stepSummary: On ערב פסח the afternoon תמיד is slaughtered at 7½ and offered at 8½. This is the same whether ערב פסח falls on a weekday or on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב פסח, it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours and offered at eight and a half hours, whether that day is a weekday or שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us that on ערב פסח the whole תמיד schedule shifts one hour earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח must be brought after the afternoon תמיד, and huge numbers of people must slaughter their פסח. So the תמיד is moved up an hour to leave time. The משנה adds that this applies even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The eves of פסח, the 14th of ניסן
Whether on a weekday or on שבת

phrases.english: On the eves of Passover it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours,
and offered at eight and a half hours —
whether on a weekday or on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a special-day adjustment to the regular schedule in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב פסח, weekday or שבת, the תמיד is slaughtered at 7½ and offered at 8½.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line becomes the basis of רבא's challenge in step 6.

steps.title: When ערב פסח falls on Friday, it moves even earlier
steps.stepSummary: If ערב פסח falls on ערב שבת, the תמיד is slaughtered at 6½ and offered at 7½, and the קרבן פסח is brought after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ערב פסח falls on Friday, the תמיד is slaughtered at six and a half hours and offered at seven and a half, and the קרבן פסח comes after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third schedule for when ערב פסח is on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Friday the קרבן פסח must also be roasted before שבת begins, since roasting is not allowed on שבת. So the תמיד moves up another hour to give extra time. The order stays the same: תמיד first, then פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
And the קרבן פסח comes after it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three schedules: regular (8½ and 9½), ערב פסח (7½ and 8½), and ערב פסח on Friday (6½ and 7½). In every case the פסח comes after the תמיד.

phrases.aramaic: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: If Passover eve falls on Shabbat eve,
it is slaughtered at six and a half hours,
and offered at seven and a half hours,
and the Paschal lamb after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further adjustment on top of the ערב פסח schedule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ערב פסח is on Friday, the תמיד is slaughtered at 6½ and offered at 7½, and then the פסח is brought.

steps.title: What is the source for the regular time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the afternoon תמיד belongs at 8½ to 9½ hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the Torah source of the משנה's regular time. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is aimed at the baseline time in step 1, not the special ערב פסח times. The גמרא wants to see how the Torah points to exactly 8½ to 9½ hours.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
From where do we know these things? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for slaughtering the afternoon תמיד at 8½ hours and offering it at 9½.

steps.title: Splitting the afternoon into two 'evenings'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'בין הערבים' as 'between the two evenings'. He divides the afternoon into 2½ hours, then 2½ hours, with one hour in the middle for the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The verse says, 'One lamb you shall offer in the morning and the second lamb you shall offer בין הערבים, between the evenings.' Divide the afternoon between two 'evenings': two and a half hours on this side, two and a half hours on that side, and one hour in the middle for doing it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question by explaining a פסוק about the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The afternoon runs from midday, the 6th hour, to sunset, the 12th hour, which is 6 hours. 'בין הערבים' means 'between the evenings', so he makes two 'evening' blocks of 2½ hours each and leaves 1 hour between them. That middle hour runs from 8½ to 9½, which is exactly the משנה's time.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
Literally 'between the evenings'; the afternoon
Divide it
For performing it, the time to bring the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: If this hour comes from a Torah verse, it seems fixed by Torah law. That is exactly what רבא attacks next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
as the verse says:
"The one lamb you shall offer in the morning

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵת הַכֶּבֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִי תַּעֲשֶׂה בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: and the second lamb you shall offer between the evenings,"
divide it between two evenings:
two and a half hours on this side,
two and a half hours on that side,
and one hour for performing it.
phrases.notes: 6 + 2½ = 8½ and 12 − 2½ = 9½, so the middle hour runs from 8½ to 9½.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'בין הערבים' splits the six afternoon hours into two 2½-hour 'evenings', with the middle hour, 8½ to 9½, set aside for the תמיד.

steps.title: If the time is from the Torah, how can it move earlier?
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה's ערב פסח schedule. If 8½ hours is required by Torah law, how could we ever slaughter the תמיד earlier?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: The משנה says that on ערב פסח the תמיד is slaughtered at 7½ and offered at 8½, whether on a weekday or שבת. If you think 8½ hours is required by Torah law, how can we move it earlier?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי, using the משנה's own ruling about ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי made 8½ to 9½ sound like a Torah-fixed window. But the משנה lets us slaughter at 7½ on ערב פסח, outside that window, and even on שבת. Moving a Torah-set time just to make room for the פסח seems impossible, so the derivation looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind, meaning 'if you think that'
By Torah law
We move it earlier

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not making a new rule here. He is re-quoting the משנה from step 2 and using it as a weapon against the derivation in step 5.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
On the eves of Passover it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours,
and offered at eight and a half hours —
whether on a weekday or on Shabbat!
And if it enters your mind
that eight and a half hours is by Torah law,
how can we move it earlier?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation of step 5 using the משנה ruling of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim that the 8½ to 9½ window comes from the Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah-fixed time could not be moved earlier for convenience. Yet the משנה moves the תמיד to 7½ on ערב פסח, even on שבת, so the time cannot be a strict Torah requirement.

steps.title: רבא's new source: the תמיד's time begins when the sun starts going down
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets aside רבי יהושע בן לוי's source. He says the Torah time for the afternoon תמיד starts when the evening shadows begin to lean, because 'בין הערבים' means from when the sun starts to go west.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the מצוה of the afternoon תמיד begins once the evening shadows start to lean. Why? Because the verse says 'בין הערבים', meaning from the time the sun starts to set.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the problem he raised in step 6. He gives a new reading of the verse so the Torah time for the תמיד is no longer locked at 8½ hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading fixed the תמיד at 8½ hours. That made it impossible to bring it earlier on ערב פסח. רבא reads 'ערב' as the moment the sun begins its descent, right after midday, so the Torah window opens much earlier and an earlier slaughter is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a signal that the earlier approach is being dropped
From when the evening shadows begin to lean, just after midday
'In the afternoon', the Torah's phrase for the time of the afternoon תמיד
To go down in the west, to begin setting

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is arguing about practice. Everyone agrees the תמיד is usually brought at 8½ hours. רבא only changes what the Torah requires, which is a window that opens much earlier.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one reading changes the 8½ hours from a Torah requirement into a scheduling choice. The rest of the סוגיא builds on that.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means רבי יהושע בן לוי's source is set aside.

phrases.english: The מצוה of the daily offering
phrases.notes: Here this means the afternoon תמיד.

phrases.english: is from when the evening shadows lean.
phrases.notes: After midday the sun moves west, so shadows lean east.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says: 'In the afternoon',
meaning from the time the sun begins to set.
phrases.notes: 'ערב' is read as the start of the sun's descent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from step 6 by replacing the source from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New derivation from the verse (replaces the earlier source)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the Torah fixes the תמיד at 8½ hours, so an earlier slaughter would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah time begins right after midday, so 8½ hours is not required by the Torah.

steps.title: Why the תמיד is usually delayed to 8½ hours
steps.stepSummary: On ordinary days the many vow and gift offerings must be brought before the afternoon תמיד. A דרשה teaches this: 'עליה' means all offerings are completed on top of the morning תמיד. So the afternoon תמיד is pushed back two hours, to 8½.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, on the rest of the year's days, when there are vow offerings and gift offerings, since the Torah said 'עליה חלבי השלמים', and the Master explained that 'upon it' means complete all the offerings upon it, we delay the תמיד two hours and bring it at 8½.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the Torah time starts early, the גמרא explains why the usual practice is 8½ hours. It is a practical delay to leave room for other offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other offerings may not come after the afternoon תמיד. The verse 'עליה' teaches that everything is finished between the morning תמיד and the afternoon one. Since many private offerings must fit into that time, we push the afternoon תמיד two hours later than its earliest time, from 6½ to 8½.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, applying the rule just stated
Vow offerings and gift offerings, which are voluntary sacrifices
'Upon it, complete', meaning all offerings are finished after the morning תמיד
The fats of the שלמים offerings
We delay

steps.confusionAlert: 'עליה' does not only mean 'on the altar'. The דרשה reads it as 'after it', meaning after the morning תמיד, with everything done before the afternoon one.

phrases.english: Therefore, on the rest of the days of the year,
when there are vow offerings and gift offerings,
since the Merciful One said: 'upon it the fats of the peace-offerings',
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא ו:ה, talking about the morning עולה.

phrases.english: and the Master said ('upon it the fats of the peace-offerings'):
'upon it' complete all the offerings, every one —
phrases.notes: A wordplay: שְׁלָמִים is read as הַשְׁלֵם, 'complete'.

phrases.english: so we delay it two hours,
phrases.notes: Two hours past its earliest time of 6½.

phrases.english: and perform it at eight and a half hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's early Torah time to explain the usual 8½ practice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical explanation of a rabbinic or scheduling delay
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 8½ hours looked like the Torah's fixed time.
steps.terutzMaskana: 8½ hours is a two-hour delay made to fit in the other offerings.

steps.title: On ערב פסח the תמיד is moved one hour earlier
steps.stepSummary: On ערב פסח the קרבן פסח must come after the תמיד. So we shorten the delay by one hour and bring the תמיד at 7½.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the eves of פסח, when there is the קרבן פסח after it, we move it up one hour and bring it at 7½.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first time in the משנה (step 2). The ערב פסח time of 7½ comes from shortening the usual delay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole nation's קרבן פסח must be slaughtered after the afternoon תמיד. That needs a lot of time before dark. So instead of a two-hour delay we use only one hour, landing at 7½. This is allowed because the Torah window already opened at 6½.

keyTerms.meaning: The eves of פסח, the 14th of ניסן
The קרבן פסח that is brought after the תמיד
We move it earlier

phrases.english: On the eves of Passover,
when there is the Paschal offering after it,
we advance it one hour,
phrases.notes: One hour earlier than the usual 8½.

phrases.english: and perform it at seven and a half hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the 8½ schedule from step 8 for ערב פסח, answering רבא's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shortening a delay that was never required by the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bringing the תמיד at 7½ seemed to go against the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: 7½ falls inside the Torah window. We simply delay one hour instead of two.

steps.title: When ערב פסח falls on ערב שבת, the תמיד goes back to its basic time of 6½
steps.stepSummary: If ערב פסח is on Friday, the קרבן פסח must also be roasted before שבת, because roasting does not override שבת. So there is no delay at all, and the תמיד is brought at its basic time of 6½.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ערב פסח falls on ערב שבת, when there is also its roasting, which does not push aside שבת, we keep the תמיד at its basic law: 6½ hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last case in the משנה (step 3), the Friday ערב פסח. This finishes רבא's full explanation of the three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering the פסח overrides שבת, but roasting it does not. So all the roasting must be done before שבת starts. That means even more time is needed, so we drop the delay completely and bring the תמיד at the earliest Torah time, 6½.

keyTerms.meaning: Its roasting, meaning the roasting of the קרבן פסח
Overrides שבת, pushes aside the שבת prohibitions
At its basic law, its original Torah time

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law the afternoon תמיד may be brought from 6½ hours. Ordinary days: delayed two hours to 8½, to leave room for other offerings. ערב פסח: delayed only one hour, to 7½, for the קרבן פסח. ערב פסח on ערב שבת: no delay, 6½, because the roasting must finish before שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix these up. Slaughtering the פסח does override שבת, but roasting it does not. That is why only a Friday ערב פסח needs the extra time.

phrases.aramaic: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: If Passover eve falls on Shabbat eve,
when there is also its roasting
which does not override Shabbat —
we set it at its basic law, at six and a half hours.
phrases.notes: This is the earliest Torah time, with no delay at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the schedule by explaining the Friday case from the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three times in the משנה fit רבא's reading. The Torah time begins at 6½, and each later time is just a practical delay.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the תמיד schedule on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל says the תמיד is arranged on שבת just like on a weekday. רבי עקיבא says it is arranged like on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Its arrangement on שבת is just like its arrangement on a weekday.' These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: 'Like its arrangement on ערב פסח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, about when the afternoon תמיד is brought on שבת. It records two opinions that are worded very briefly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions are short and do not say which weekday or which שבת they mean. Does 'weekday' mean an ordinary day or ערב פסח? Is this any שבת or a שבת that is ערב פסח? The rest of the סוגיא clears up this vagueness, starting in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrangement or schedule. Here it means the timing of the afternoon תמיד.
A weekday, meaning a day that is not שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Like its arrangement on a weekday,
so is its arrangement on Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Like its arrangement on Erev Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ordinary, ערב פסח, and Friday ערב פסח schedules to a ברייתא about שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל compares the שבת schedule to a weekday, and רבי עקיבא compares it to ערב פסח.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is actually saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear ברייתא. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The wording is too short to tell which situations are being compared. As written, an ordinary weekday and an ordinary שבת would have the same schedule anyway, so the dispute needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he saying?' A request to explain unclear wording.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which days are being compared in each opinion of the ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי's reading: both opinions are about ערב פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, רבי ישמעאל says ערב פסח on שבת is like ערב פסח on a weekday (7½). רבי עקיבא says it is like ערב פסח on Friday (6½). Our משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said that this is what it means. 'Like its arrangement on ערב פסח that falls on a weekday, so is its arrangement on ערב פסח that falls on שבת.' These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: 'Like its arrangement on ערב פסח that falls on Friday, so is its arrangement on שבת.' So our משנה, which says 'whether on a weekday or on שבת,' follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fills in the missing words. In his reading, both תנאים are talking about ערב פסח that falls on שבת. They only disagree about which earlier case it resembles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, ערב פסח on שבת is like any weekday ערב פסח, so the תמיד is at 7½. For רבי עקיבא, it is like ערב פסח on Friday, so the תמיד is at 6½. Our משנה gives the same 7½ for weekday and שבת, so it must follow רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he means.' This introduces a reinterpretation of a text.
'That happens to fall on' a certain day.
Our משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: In אביי's reading, the word 'weekday' in רבי ישמעאל's opinion does NOT mean an ordinary day. It means ערב פסח that falls on a weekday.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
Like its arrangement on Erev Pesach that falls on a weekday,
so is its arrangement on Erev Pesach that falls on Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Like its arrangement on Erev Pesach
that falls on Erev Shabbat,
so is its arrangement on Shabbat.
And our Mishnah, which teaches
'whether on a weekday or on Shabbat' (7½),
follows Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by filling in the missing words of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both opinions are about ערב פסח on שבת. רבי ישמעאל says 7½ and רבי עקיבא says 6½. The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: Following אביי's reading, the גמרא asks what underlying issue the two תנאים disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the מחלוקת in אביי's reading. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the two times (7½ and 6½) are clear, we need to know why they differ. On שבת there are no voluntary offerings to cause a delay, so something else must explain the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they disagree?' A request for the underlying principle of a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's reading and asks for the reasoning behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that leads רבי ישמעאל to 7½ and רבי עקיבא to 6½.

steps.title: Do the מוספין or the בזיכין come first?
steps.stepSummary: They disagree about the order of the extra שבת services. רבי ישמעאל puts the מוספין first (6, then בזיכין at 7, then תמיד at 7½). רבי עקיבא puts the בזיכין first (5, then מוספין at 6, then תמיד at 6½).
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about whether the מוספין come before the בזיכין. רבי ישמעאל holds that the מוספין come first. The כהן brings the מוספין at six hours, the בזיכין at seven, and the תמיד at seven and a half. רבי עקיבא holds that the בזיכין come first. The בזיכין are at five, the מוספין at six, and the תמיד at six and a half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that on שבת two extra services must happen before the afternoon תמיד: the מוספין and the burning of the בזיכין. Their order decides when the תמיד can be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the מוספין are brought at six hours. If the מוספין come first, the בזיכין are pushed to seven and the תמיד to 7½. If the בזיכין come first, they can be done at five, so after the מוספין at six the תמיד is brought right away at 6½.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional offerings brought on שבת and יום טוב.
The bowls of frankincense that sat with the לחם הפנים all week. They were burned on the מזבח on שבת.
Come first, take precedence.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, in אביי's reading, the delay of the תמיד on שבת is caused by the order of the extra שבת services, not by voluntary offerings.

phrases.english: They disagree about whether the additional offerings precede the frankincense bowls.
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
The additional offerings precede the bowls.
He brings the additional offerings at six hours,
and the bowls at seven,
and he brings the Tamid at seven and a half.
Rabbi Akiva holds:
The bowls precede the additional offerings.
The bowls at five,
and the additional offerings at six,
and he brings the Tamid at six and a half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 with the underlying principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is about the order of the מוספין and the בזיכין, and that order determines when the תמיד is brought.

steps.title: רבא: רבי עקיבא never mentioned Friday
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי's reading. רבי עקיבא's words say only 'ערב פסח,' with nothing about ערב פסח that falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: Does רבי עקיבא say 'like its arrangement on ערב פסח that falls on Friday'? He says simply 'like its arrangement on ערב פסח,' without any detail!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation because it adds words to רבי עקיבא's opinion that are not in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read רבי עקיבא as referring to the special Friday case (6½). But רבי עקיבא's words are plain and general: 'ערב פסח.' Plain words should mean the normal ערב פסח, not a rare case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He strongly challenged it.' A sharp objection to a previous explanation.
'Does it teach this at all?' A rhetorical way of saying the text does not say that.
Plainly, without further detail.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to this:
Does Rabbi Akiva
teach 'like its arrangement on Erev Pesach
that falls on Erev Shabbat'?!
He teaches simply 'like its arrangement on Erev Pesach,' without detail.

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's interpretation of רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The interpretation adds a detail ('falls on Friday') that the ברייתא's plain wording does not contain.

steps.title: רבא's reading: ordinary weekday versus regular ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי ישמעאל compares ערב פסח on שבת to an ordinary weekday (8½). רבי עקיבא compares it to a regular ערב פסח (7½). Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said that this is what it means. 'Like its arrangement on an ordinary weekday, so is its arrangement on שבת that is ערב פסח.' These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: 'Like its arrangement on ערב פסח.' So our משנה, which says 'whether on a weekday or on שבת,' follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different reading that keeps רבי עקיבא's words plain. As a result, our משנה now matches רבי עקיבא instead of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, ערב פסח on שבת gets no early schedule. The תמיד is at the ordinary time of 8½. For רבי עקיבא, it is like any ערב פסח, so the תמיד is at 7½. That matches our משנה, which gives 7½ for both weekday and שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' This drops the previous explanation and introduces a new one.
An ordinary weekday, not ערב פסח.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: רבי ישמעאל says 7½ and רבי עקיבא says 6½ (based on whether the מוספין or the בזיכין come first). The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל. רבא: רבי ישמעאל says 8½ and רבי עקיבא says 7½. The משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבא's reading, 'weekday' in רבי ישמעאל's opinion means an ordinary day. In אביי's reading it meant ערב פסח on a weekday. The same words are read in opposite ways.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: This is what it is saying:
Like its arrangement on an ordinary weekday,
so is its arrangement on Shabbat that is Erev Pesach,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Like its arrangement on Erev Pesach.
phrases.notes: That is, 7½ hours, as on a weekday ערב פסח.

phrases.english: And our Mishnah, which teaches
'whether on a weekday or on Shabbat,'
follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's reading after the objection in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא that keeps רבי עקיבא's words plain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי: רבי עקיבא refers to ערב פסח on Friday (6½), and the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא: רבי ישמעאל says ordinary weekday timing (8½) and רבי עקיבא says regular ערב פסח timing (7½). The משנה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: What is the reason behind their argument in רבא's reading?
steps.stepSummary: Following רבא's reading, the גמרא asks what underlying issue the two תנאים disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא's disagreement, now that we are using רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא asked this same question about אביי's reading. The answer there was the order of the extra שבת services. Now that רבא has changed what each תנא says (8½ versus 7½), a new explanation is needed for why they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (a request for the root reason behind an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: The same question the גמרא asked in step 14, now asked about רבא's reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two positions that רבא laid out in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle explains why רבי ישמעאל compares ערב פסח on שבת to a weekday (8½), while רבי עקיבא compares it to a regular ערב פסח (7½)?

steps.title: They disagree about whether to worry that the meat will spoil
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is about the worry that the meat will get warm and spoil. רבי ישמעאל is worried about this, so he does not move the schedule earlier. רבי עקיבא is not worried, so he keeps the early ערב פסח schedule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the meat becoming warm and spoiling. רבי ישמעאל holds that we are worried the meat will become warm and spoil. רבי עקיבא holds that we are not worried the meat will become warm and spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The argument depends on whether we worry that the meat of the קרבן פסח will spoil while it waits to be roasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular ערב פסח, the תמיד is moved earlier to leave time to slaughter the many קרבנות פסח that come after it (step 9). On שבת, however, the meat cannot be roasted until שבת ends, so a פסח slaughtered early would sit for hours and might spoil. רבי ישמעאל worries about this, so he keeps the late weekday schedule (8½). רבי עקיבא does not worry, so he keeps the usual early ערב פסח schedule (7½).

keyTerms.meaning: The meat becoming warm and spoiling
We are concerned / we take this worry into account
We are not concerned / we do not worry about it
He holds (his opinion is)
Roasting (forbidden on שבת, so the פסח must wait until night)

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's reading, the argument was about the order of the שבת services. In רבא's reading, it is about whether we worry the meat of the פסח will spoil before it can be roasted after שבת. רבי ישמעאל worries, so he says 8½. רבי עקיבא does not worry, so he says 7½, and our משנה follows him.
steps.confusionAlert: The meat is not spoiling because of anything wrong with the slaughter. It is simply waiting for hours, because roasting is not allowed on שבת. The only question is whether this waiting time is a real concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two readings of the ברייתא (אביי's and רבא's) each lead to a completely different root reason for the argument.

phrases.english: They disagree about the meat becoming warm and spoiling.
phrases.notes: This is the general answer. The details of each side follow.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: חָיְישִׁינַן לְמִכְמַר בִּשְׂרָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds: we are concerned lest the meat become warm and spoil.
phrases.notes: So he does not slaughter early on שבת, and the תמיד stays at 8½.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְמִכְמַר בִּשְׂרָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds: we are not concerned lest the meat become warm and spoil.
phrases.notes: So he keeps the regular early ערב פסח schedule, with the תמיד at 7½.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is about whether we worry that the slaughtered meat will spoil while it waits until after שבת to be roasted. רבי ישמעאל worries about it; רבי עקיבא does not.
